description.value: A double-blind functional MRI study examining whether primary somatosensory cortex activity induced by reflexological stimulation is affected by correct versus pseudo-information about the stimulated reflex area, and examining stimulation laterality.

spans.text: The present experiment was a double-blind study.

description.value: Double-blind, repeated-measures fMRI experiment in which healthy volunteers received correct or pseudo-information about reflex areas on the second and third toes, followed by stimulation of both feet. The data were analyzed with a two-stage approach using subject-level GLMs and group-level repeated-measures ANOVA.

spans.text: The fMRI experiment was conducted using a block design consisting of four sensory stimulation tasks that involved stimulating the base of the second or third toes of subjects’ feet.

One factor was the laterality of the stimulated reflex area (left or right; two conditions), and the other factor was the accuracy of the assigned reflex-area information (correct or pseudo; two conditions).
The present experiment was a double-blind study.

description.value: fMRI preprocessing in SPM8 included realignment, coregistration of the structural image to the mean EPI, spatial normalization to the MNI-T1 template, and Gaussian spatial smoothing.

spans.text: The structural image volume was then co-registered with the mean image of realigned echo-planar image (EPI). All EPI were spatially normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI)-T1 template using the parameter to co-register and to normalize the structural image for the MNI-T1 template obtained by a segmentation process for each subject. Finally, each scan was smoothed with a Gaussian filter in a spatial domain (8-mm full-width at half maximum).
Data preprocessing and statistical analyses of the fMRI data were carried out using statistical parametric mapping software (SPM8; Wellcome Trust Center for Neuroimaging, London, UK).

model_type.value: general linear model with multiple regression

spans.text: A multiple regression analysis was performed on each voxel to detect the regions where MR signal changes were correlated with the hypothesized model to obtain the partial regression coefficients of each voxel.
The hemodynamic response was assumed to be the canonical hemodynamic response function of 5-s duration.

model_settings.value: Global intensity normalization and high-pass filtering with a 128-s cutoff.

spans.text: Global intensity normalization was performed on the average within-brain fMRI signal in each image, and low-frequency confounding effects were removed using a high-pass filter with a 128-s cutoff.
